79102.subject: Data & Insights: Everyone is fomoing; AI Coins Spike
79102.body:
The Data and Insights newsletter brings the highlights of the week from The Block’s Data Dashboard

( https://www.theblock.co/data/crypto-markets/spot )

Presented by:

Fidelity ( https://jobs.fidelity.com/en/crypto-careers/?utm_source=theblock&utm_medium=paidsocial&utm_campaign=jobssocial&utm_content=awn-cry-datainsights-s )

GM, data bulls! Happy Clarity Week! Let's see if the industry gets its monumental legislation this week. Our team recently sent out Issue 1 ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters/tokenization-briefing ) of our a new newsletter titled "Tokenization Briefing." With trillions of dollars of real-world assets migrating onto blockchain rails, we are introducing a way for readers to keep up to date with market insights and visual analyses on what matters in the world of Tokenization. Sign up here ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters ) to get Issue Two tomorrow.

This week, we’re taking a look at fomo's App Store climb and AI token prices. We’ll also look at how Robinhood Chain is doing as well as an OG Solana DEX's comeback. So grab a drink, take a seat, and let's dive in.

1: Ahhh I'm Fomoing

( https://www.theblock.co/data/alternative-crypto-metrics/app-usage/crypto-apps-ranking-on-the-app-store-in-the-us-finance-category )

Chart via The Block's Data Dashboard

*Key Insights* provided by The Block Research

* fomo, the crypto social trading mobile app, climbed to No.32 in the US App Store's Finance category last Tuesday, the best ranking the app has ever had.

* It now ranks ahead of Coinbase, which sat at No. 55 that day.

* fomo's trading capabilities offersnusers a single interface to trade onchain tokens across multiple chains such as Ethereum, Solana, Base, BNB Chain and Robinhood Chain.

* The app generated $13.8 million of revenue in August, with an annualized run rate of roughly $165.6 million, and recorded a single-day high of $1.1 million on September 1st.
* It is undoubtedly one of, if not THE, breakout crypto app of the year.
* Though it is worth noting that the trader base behind these metrics is fairly wide and thin.
* Roughly 101K  daily active users traded in the most recent week, with ~95% of them having either lost money or earning less than $100.
* Meanwhile, only 229 traders, 0.06% of the cohort, cleared over $10K in profits.

79099.subject: ⏸️ People building AI want to slow down, except one
79099.body:
The Atlas

Автор: GenAI Works


Автор: GenAI Works

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/people-building-ai-want-slow-down-except-one-genai-works-v9qcf?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BfyX0LoWpSb6BnLkCGMvyiA%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=3kaMYS9FZe4ss1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mu1dgcq4~47-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mu1dgcq4-47
  
Welcome back! Amodei asked the industry to hit the brakes and got Altman, Musk and Nadella nodding along. One CEO went the other way and started opening weights.  In today's Atlas Newsletter: Everyone agreed to slow down except Zuckerberg: What does Amodei think happens in the next 6 to 12 months? Goldmine for AI Engineers: Which repo do people skip, then blame the math three weeks later? Stop downloading LLMs your machine was never going to run: How do you know before the download finishes? Start studying this paper right now instead of talking about Astra: What happens when a Transformer runs its middle layers twice? PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. Everyone agreed to slow down except Zuckerberg Dario Amodei published an essay asking the AI industry to slow down, and Sam Altman agreed with him in public. Amodei's argument is that the rogue agent swarm that hit OpenAI and Hugging Face could have been far worse.  He puts a timeline on the next one: within 6 to 12 months a swarm like that could take the internet with a persistent botnet and do hundreds of billions in damage. Anthropic went past the essay and changed its access policy.  Outside safety testers now get desks, badges, company laptops and the right to publish what they find without Anthropic reviewing it first.  Altman said OpenAI will match that, and that nobody at a frontier lab should bother showing up to work if they cannot promise the public that much. Elon Musk backed the essay.  Satya Nadella called for deliberate pacing. Mark Zuckerberg watched all of it and went the other direction. His position has not moved since his August manifesto.  Any policy that slows American model releases, even by a month, cedes ground to foreign labs.  He says he worries more about AI power ending up inside one government or one company than about the specific risks the safety side keeps naming. So Meta is opening the weights of a model called Muse Glimmer, with a version of Muse Spark 1.2 to follow. The interesting part is that Altman named concentration of power as one of his two nightmares too.  Both men identify the same danger and split on whether shipping faster fixes it or creates it. The essay has skeptics on both flanks.  Chamath Palihapitiya read it as a play to kill open sourc

79093.subject: Bartleby: Meetings are broccoli
79093.body:
The Economist Picks

Автор: The Economist


Автор: The Economist

A long long time ago, when Manchester United was a genuinely successful football club, a group of researchers wondered whether being a fan of the team would affect someone’s willingness to help a supporter of a rival outfit. Their experiment can teach managers something about group identities at work, the subject of this week’s Bartleby column.   And my weekly newsletter for subscribers looks at a paper that asks why meetings are both so disliked and so persistent. Broccoli supplies the answer. You can sign up to read that here.   Andrew Palmer, Bartleby columnist Latest column Are you committed to your company or your team? Employees have overlapping identities at work. That’s a challenge for bosses Humans are conditioned to form allegiances extremely quickly, a type of behaviour sometimes called the “minimal group effect”. In a famous series of experiments, a social psychologist called Henri Tajfel found that you can divide strangers into groups on totally arbitrary grounds—how good they are at estimating the number of dots on a chart, say, or how much they like a certain type of abstract art, or even just on the basis of a coin toss—and they will immediately start to favour members of their own group when then asked to distribute rewards. From the Boss Class vault Innovation: Coming up with new ideas Forget the whiteboards, hammocks and ping-pong tables How do the world’s biggest firms develop their best ideas? At Google, whose flagship product is threatened by artificial intelligence, that question is urgent. Liz Reid’s job is to find the answer. On our “Boss Class” podcast the tech giant’s head of search explains how she develops ideas. Elsewhere in The Economist ▸ Should Anthropic press pause on a potential $2trn IPO? ▸ The new age of the orator ▸ Are teenagers growing dimmer? Enjoying this newsletter? If you’re a subscriber you can get it in your inbox every Monday by signing up here. You’ll get more on work and office life from our management columnist.

79091.subject: Pump Strikes Back
79091.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

Happy Monday. Every major benchmark closed the week lower as hot core CPI and $100 oil pushed the odds of a hike at this week's Fed meeting to 87%, Trump signed off on an ethics provision that gives the Clarity Act its best odds since July, and on Solana a launchpad that matched Pump.fun's revenue in a week got its best features copied the next week. 

In today's edition, we discuss the sell-off into the Fed decision and the fight between StonkFun and Pump.fun.

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/42e942ec-f31d-4957-8722-a3ac7b121e1e/0xR_NL_Market_Update.png?t=1767631151) [Market Update]
Caption: 

All four major benchmarks finished the week in the red. The S&P 500 fell 1.4%, while the Nasdaq and gold both declined 2.4%. BTC was the weakest performer, ending the week down 4.5%.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/30c3b98f-fda5-4537-9000-04c7f0c3dbe6/image.png?t=1789378893)
Caption: 

As covered in Friday’s [edition](https://blockworks.com/newsletter/0xresearch), the sell-off has been driven by rising expectations for further rate hikes. Core CPI increased 0.3% MoM, above expectations, while WTI continues to trade around $100. Markets now [price](https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html) an 86.7% chance of a hike at this week’s Fed meeting and a 25% chance of three hikes by the end of 2026.

The major crypto [news](https://apnews.com/article/donald-trump-cryptocurrency-ethics-521fd5986eb107413064018f7a468c51) this morning is that Trump has agreed to a new bipartisan ethics provision in the proposed Clarity Act, which is heading for a key vote this week. The revised rules would allow state attorneys general to enforce restrictions preventing federal officials from issuing, sponsoring or holding significant interests in digital assets. They could also act against exchanges that list assets in violation of those restrictions.

The development has pushed the odds of the Clarity Act becoming law in 2026 to [32%](https://polymarket.com/event/clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026), their highest level since late July. For anyone wondering what the bill could mean for the digital asset industry, I could not recommend this [read](https://app.blockworksresearch.com/research/how-clarity-reshapes-crypto-regulation) more.

The weakness extended across crypto, with every sector we track finishing the week deep in the red except Gaming, which ended roughly flat.
